subject: fisher
title: A 10-Pound Animal Kills Porcupines, and It Only Attacks One Spot

scenes.text: A porcupine has 30,000 quills. One animal found the gap.
The fisher is a ten-pound weasel from the forests of North America. It eats mice, hares, and porcupines.
The porcupine backs against a tree and swings its tail. The fisher circles. Then it strikes the only part without quills: the face.
Bite, retreat, bite again. When the porcupine can no longer defend itself, the fisher flips it over and opens the soft belly.
It can do this up a tree, because its hind feet rotate almost 180 degrees so it climbs down head first.
It is not perfect. In Maine, up to two thirds of males carry quills, some over a hundred. They keep hunting anyway.

description:
The fisher, a large weasel of about 10 to 12 pounds, is one of the only predators that routinely kills porcupines. It attacks the face, the one part of a porcupine with no quills, again and again, then flips the animal over to reach the unprotected underside.
Its hind feet rotate almost 180 degrees, letting it climb down trees head first and catch porcupines in the branches. Maine wildlife biologists report that up to two thirds of male fishers carry embedded quills, some more than 100, with no apparent harm to their health.
Would you take on 30,000 quills for dinner? Comment below.
first_comment: Despite the name, fishers eat almost no fish. Which predator with a signature move should we cover next?
